rv.q: The result is a lucid, delightfully ironic and politically piercing 80 minutes that combine comedy, honesty and protest to distinctive effect.
This is a show with a very clear message yet it's really very gentle – sometimes a little too gentle.
Hammond and Spence are sincere, incessantly funny and have the rapport perfectly suited to leaping from humour to pathos in a matter of minutes.

To the recent spate of shows that put their own narrative-building first, we can now add Still No Idea , with the addendum that this self-penned two-hander may be the funniest and fiercest of them all to date.

cn.t: Hammond and Spence deliver a spiky, funny exploration of public attitudes toward disability that proves both politically pointed and delightfully ironic, blending stand-up, verbatim theatre, and improv with lucid wit.
